key_insight: Quantum machine learning offers experimental approaches to medical imaging, but this review finds that clinical deployment is not yet feasible.
engineering_relevance: Practical value depends on efficient data encoding, quantum algorithms, measurement strategies, and integration with classical imaging pipelines—not superposition alone.
method: Introduces core quantum concepts and superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic hardware.
Reviews quantum support vector machines, neural networks, variational circuits, and convolutional networks.
Surveys FRQI and NEQR image representations and medical imaging applications.
evidence_signal: Nearly all reported systems use hybrid quantum-classical pipelines evaluated on small, downsampled benchmark datasets or simulators.
watch_item: Results on simplified datasets or simulators do not establish a practical quantum advantage for clinical imaging.
paper_title: Quantum Machine Learning in Medical Imaging: A Primer for Radiologists
